answer: Each identity is a lotus floating on one shared karst aquifer: to stay alive it must be fed by a unique underground channel carrying verifiable work, and the aquifer yields a fixed flow. One operator running n identities splits the same flow n ways, so each lotus wilts unless the operator supplies n times the work per lotus — upkeep grows as the square of clone count. Each lotus also carries an onyx stake that burns if two channels share one operator fingerprint, so clones cannot pool water or hide behind one another.
